messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx + streaming timeouts observed in eu-west-1 across gateway cluster gw-eu-*. Rule: streaming_error_rate > 5% over 5m. Paging sara_oncall and eng-runtime.

sara_oncall: acked. I'm oncall, joining. Can someone grab initial blast radius and customer impact? @product_ops

product_ops: seeing alerts from synthetic monitors (streaming healthcheck) and first-party customers reporting truncated streams. Estimated affected sessions ~ 6-8% of streaming traffic for eu-west-1 in last 10m. No paid customers reported full outage yet but multiple regen attempts from clients.

mike_runtime: looking at runtime dashboards now. Streaming 5xx looks like Gateway returning 502/504 at the fanout stage and then the client sees early EOF. Backend model nodes are mostly green; spike seems to align with high connection churn and increased chunked-encoding resets.

ellie_sre: I grabbed gateway logs. Early signs show a lot of `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` from nginx on gw-eu-03. Also seeing TCP retransmits between gateway and fanout pool.

mike_runtime: possible correlation with kernel update on a subset of hosts? netops, did we recently push any ENI/MTU or iptables changes to eu-west? @netops

netops: No infra changes this morning in eu-west. We did patch a small number of infra instances last night but not the gateway fleet. However, cloud provider reported brief network flaps in the region ~ 05:12 UTC, matching spike start.

sara_oncall: ok, plan: 1) throttle new streaming sessions at gateway level to reduce fanout concurrency. 2) enable fallback mode that serves a lower-concurrency variant of the model (same API surface) for eu-west. 3) add additional keepalive and increase proxy timeout to avoid premature upstream closes. Implementing now, will post commands.

mike_runtime: applicable toggle: in runtime-config -> routing -> eu-west -> streaming_concurrency_limit. Setting to 0.6 of baseline (from 100 -> 60). Also enabling `fallback_variant=low_concurrency_v1` for route `/v1/stream`.

ellie_sre: running kubectl exec into gw-eu-03 to tail logs: ```
kubectl -n prod logs gw-eu-03 -f --since=10m | grep -E "upstream prematurely closed|client closed"
``` Seeing repeated blocks: ```
[error] 2026/03/15 05:14:22 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.12.8.44, server: _, request: "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.20.1.7:8080/stream", host: api.redwood.example"
```

ellie_sre: Also noticed some chunked-encoding `write ECONNRESET` on fanout side. Dumping a conntrack sample and tcpdump for 20s on gw-eu-03.

netops: tcpdump shows a burst of RST packets between gw-eu-03 and model-node-07 around 05:14:20. Possibly connection exhaustion on the model-node side.

mike_runtime: model-node-07 logs show `accept() failed: Too many open files` at 05:14:19. That points at FD exhaustion under bursty fanout. Might be combined effect: network flaps causing retries that spike FDs.

sara_oncall: mitigation steps in order implemented: A) gateway new-session throttle applied, B) route fallback enabled to low_concurrency_v1, C) increased gateway proxy_read_timeout from 30s -> 60s, D) restarted model-node-07 with ephemeral increase of ulimit (nofile) while we plan permanent fix. Monitoring.

product_ops: notifying affected customers via status page that we're investigating degraded streaming quality in eu-west. No broad data leak or model corruption. ETA to update customers in 15m.

ellie_sre: after throttle and fallback we see 5xx drop from 6% -> 1.2% within 3m. Error types changed from 502/504 to a small number of 499 (client cancels) as clients retry. Good sign.

mike_runtime: long term fix items: - audit FD usage across model-serving process, add better accept-queue backpressure, - guardrails for retries to avoid retry storms, - ensure keepalive and net timeouts tuned across gw->fanout.

netops: I'll open a ticket with cloud provider for the reported network flaps. Also scheduling a rolling reimage for model-node-07 host pool to clear kernel-level connection tables.

sara_oncall: severity: P2 (customer-impacting but partial). Handoff to eng-runtime and netops for full remediation. I'll run postmortem if impact persists or if any customer escalates to support.

mike_runtime: note: found one config bug that allowed unlimited backend connections per gateway worker when `fallback_variant` toggles occurred; creating hotfix branch to patch concurrency accounting and add a safety cap. ETA for patch: 30-45m.

ellie_sre: running a short synthetic replay from eu-west to ensure streaming stability: ```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST https://gw-eu.redwood.example/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"test"}' & done
``` Observing sustained success under throttle. We'll run more ramp tests.

product_ops: prepping a short status page update: "We are mitigating increased streaming errors in eu-west. Temporarily throttling streaming sessions and switching to lower-concurrency model variants while we investigate. No data loss. More updates in 30m." Approve? :thumbsup:

sara_oncall: approved. post it.

netops: patch job started on model-node pool to raise ulimit permanently and rotate hosts. We'll coordinate with eng-runtime to avoid triggering more churn.

mike_runtime: hotfix (concurrency cap) merged to canary and rolling to 10% traffic in eu-west. Observing no regressions after 10m. Will promote to 100% if stable.

ellie_sre: monitoring summary at 05:30 UTC: streaming 5xx in eu-west at 0.9%, client cancels up slightly (1.4%). Latency increased by ~80ms due to fallback variant but that's acceptable. No further RST bursts.

sara_oncall: handing off incident. Oncall runbook tasks assigned: eng-runtime (mike_runtime) - full root cause and patch; netops - cloud vendor follow-up + host rotations; eng-sre (ellie_sre) - validate recovery and add additional synthetic checks for chunked resets; product_ops - customer comms and support triage. If anything spikes again ping me directly.

product_ops: capturing affected customer list and support tickets for followup. Will coordinate any crediting if required.

mike_runtime: root cause hypothesis: transient cloud network flaps caused retry amplification -> FD exhaustion on a subset of model nodes -> upstream closes -> gateway 5xx. Fix path: limit per-worker backend connections, add backpressure, increase host ulimits, and tune retry/backoff logic.

sara_oncall: closing page. Please add timeline and notes in postmortem doc. If any customer escalations or further anomalies reopen paging channel. Thanks all for fast response :heart:

incident-bot: Incident resolved and marked as mitigated by sara_oncall at 3305010600. Severity P2. Postmortem requested.
